# Metadata ownership by route (U2.3)

**8 August 2026.** Generated by `metadataOwnership()` in `scripts/audit-claims.js`,
which decides ownership by comparing what each route **serves** against each
candidate source — never by reading which file looks authoritative.

Regenerate: `node scripts/audit-claims.js --json` → `metadataOwnership`.

This table exists because the same mistake was made twice: a claim was
"corrected" in `seo.js` for a route that does not read `seo.js`, and the served
string was never touched. **Find the route here before editing its metadata.**

**38 routes.** Dead `seo.js` STATIC config: **none**. Orphan entries: **none**.

## How to read it

- **`site/*.html`** — a hand-written file served straight off disk. Edit that file.
  Its `<title>` and `<meta description>` are written in the file itself;
  `seo.js` never sees the route.
- **`seo.js STATIC`** — one of the three SPA routes with no file in `/site`
  (`/itineraries`, `/booking`, `/blog`). Edit the `STATIC` map.
- **`seo.js buildHead()`** — resolved per request from the database:
  `tourSchema()` for products, `postSchema()` for blog posts. Edit the row, not
  the code.
- **`static-seo.js injectStaticSchema()`** — JSON-LD injected on the way out of
  a static file, single-sourced from `brand.js`. The page file contains none.

## The trap this closes

`seo.js` used to hold ten `STATIC` entries. Seven were for routes served from
`/site`, so they rendered nowhere — but they looked exactly like the three that
work. The `/how-it-works` title was corrected under P1.5 and was never on the
site.

`audit-claims.js` now emits a `dead-config` finding for any entry no route
consumes, and exits non-zero, so the trap cannot silently reappear.

**One caveat learned the hard way:** `STATIC["/"]` was *also* the default
title/description for every route without an entry. Deleting it as "unreachable"
made `buildHead()` throw on every SPA route — `/itineraries`, `/blog` and
`/booking` served no title, no description and no JSON-LD. The source parsed and
all 176 tests passed; only fetching the routes showed it. Those defaults are now
`DEFAULTS`, named for what they do.
